subject: AI data-use: clarifying model-improvement rights, EU transfers, and subprocessors
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@med-innovate.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@med-innovate.com, luca.bianchi@med-innovate.com
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Data-use, subprocessors & transfers for pilot — initial questions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. Legal at MedInnovate asked me to follow up with a few concrete clarifications so we can get the clinical pilot DPA over the finish line. Our main points:

1) No-training commitment: we need a firm statement that data sent through the API for the pilot will not be incorporated into model training or used to tune public models. Is Redwood able to provide a binding clause and an audit trail that proves no downstream model training occurred on our data?

2) Prompt/response ownership: we want explicit confirmation that prompts and generated responses are treated as customer content and that MedInnovate retains IP for outputs. Can you confirm that standard language?

3) Subprocessors & EU transfers: what subprocessors will touch data? We are subject to EU regulations and need to know whether transfers rely on SCCs, adequacy decisions, or something else. Is there a way to ensure data for the pilot remains in-region?

4) Evidence & retention: if we request proof that data wasn’t used for training, what form does that take (logs, hash summaries, signed attestation)? And for how long do you retain request/response payloads by default?

I’ve attached our internal checklist — but a concise, bullet-point response would be great so I can share with Legal. Happy to hop on a short follow-up if easier.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Senior Counsel, MedInnovate Health
elena.rossi@med-innovate.com

Attachments: MedInnovate_DPA_checklist_v1.pdf
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@med-innovate.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 12:37:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data-use, subprocessors & transfers for pilot — initial questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I’ll respond to each item inline and attach the DPA we typically propose for clinical pilots. Short version up front: yes, we can support a contractual no-model-training commitment for pilot data, confirm customer ownership of prompts/outputs, and provide SCC-based transfers or EU-only processing via our Private offering. Details below.

1) No-model-training: Redwood can include a no-model-training covenant (we call it a “no-derivative-training” clause) limited to the pilot dataset and timeframe. We maintain an immutable audit trail of model-training jobs and dataset manifests; for attestations we can provide signed confirmation plus log extracts showing no training job referenced your account during the pilot window. To be clear: this is distinct from telemetry for service debugging — we can put restricted-access controls on telemetry retention for your account.

2) Ownership: our standard DPA language treats customer content (prompts + responses) as customer data; we’ll add a line clarifying output ownership and permitted uses. If you need assignment language, we can include that.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: attaching the current subprocessors list (subprocessors_2026-09.csv). For EU transfers we use SCCs between Redwood and subprocessor providers. If you require data-residency, we can run the pilot on our EU Private instance (Redwood Private) so data never leaves the EU-controlled environment.

4) Evidence & retention: default request/response retention is 30 days for hosted API; we can extend or shorten this per contract. Evidence options: (a) signed attestation + training-job logs (b) hash-chain snapshots of retained payloads with timestamps (c) short-lived exportable logs for your auditors. We typically deliver evidence as PDF attestation plus CSV log extracts, redacting unrelated operational noise.

Attaching: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf and subprocessors_2026-09.csv.

If helpful, Marcus can propose exact DPA clause wording, and Karthik can outline the runtime controls for EU-only processing. Want to set a 30-minute sync tomorrow?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Director, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, subprocessors_2026-09.csv
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@med-innovate.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@med-innovate.com, luca.bianchi@med-innovate.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 08:21:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Data-use, subprocessors & transfers for pilot — initial questions

Rachel — thanks, that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from our privacy lead:

- On the no-derivative-training attestation: will the attestation cover model checkpoints and any offline retraining processes across Redwood-managed infrastructure? We need the scope to include any derivative usage that could leak MedInnovate input/outputs into future model versions.

- On telemetry/exceptions: you mentioned telemetry for debugging. Can that telemetry be excluded from any training or aggregated-only and retained separately? Our preference is telemetry that includes customer identifiers be quarantined and not eligible for model consumption.

- Evidence format: our auditors prefer a hash-chain summary + signed attestation. Is that something Redwood can commit to producing on request, with a guaranteed turnaround (e.g., 5 business days)?

Finally, can you confirm whether SCCs are applied both for Redwood’s contracts with subprocessors and for any third-party model libraries you deploy (e.g., inference kernels run on partner cloud GPUs)? We need a clear map of transfer mechanisms.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Elena
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@med-innovate.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data-use, subprocessors & transfers for pilot — initial questions

Hi Elena — quick technical clarifications from engineering/infra side. Short answers first: yes, we can scope the attestation to include checkpoints and offline retraining; yes, telemetry can be isolated; yes, we can produce a hash-chain summary within 5 business days as a standard addendum. More detail: 

- Scope of attestation: our training pipeline records dataset manifests, job IDs, and model-checkpoint references. For contractual attestations we will run a search across training-job metadata for any reference to your account IDs and export a signed manifest showing zero matches during the specified window. That manifest will state explicitly that no weight updates, finetuning jobs, or self-supervised ingestion included your data.

- Telemetry: we categorize telemetry as (1) operational logs (health/metrics) and (2) payload telemetry (traces that include request IDs or request hashes). We can route payload telemetry for your account into a segregated retention bucket with deny-listing for training ingestion. Operational logs may remain aggregated for platform metrics but will be scrubbed of identifiable customer payloads.

- Hash-chain evidence: we can produce a Merkle-hash style summary of stored payload checksums with timestamps and sign the summary. That satisfies auditors who want tamper-evident proof without exposing raw PII. We’ll include an internal SLA of 5 business days for an evidence package request in the DPA addendum.

- SCCs and subprocessors: Redwood applies SCCs where transfers leave the EEA under the outbound transfer flow. For cloud partners that operate EU zones, we can deploy using EU-only networking and storage (no cross-border egress). Where we use a third-party subprocessor located outside the EEA, we contractually require SCCs and contractual restrictions on processing. We maintain a subprocessor map and exportable PDF we can share with you.

If you’d like, I can attach a short diagram showing where data flows for Hosted API vs Private EU deployment.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Manager, Infrastructure Product
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@med-innovate.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data-use, subprocessors & transfers for pilot — initial questions

Elena — following up with proposed contractual language and next steps. Below is a draft clause we’re comfortable with for the pilot; we can add it as an addendum to Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf and circulate a DocuSign envelope once you confirm.

DRAFT ADDENDUM (summary):
- No-derivative-training: For the duration of the pilot (start date — end date), Redwood covenants not to use any Customer Content (as defined in Section 1 of the DPA) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning model used in Redwood’s public or internal services. This covenant explicitly includes model checkpoint creation and offline retraining pipelines.

- Telemetry segregation: Redwood will segregate payload telemetry for Customer and will not include such telemetry in any model-training pipeline. Operational metrics may be retained in aggregated, non-identifiable form.

- Evidence & SLA: Upon Customer request, Redwood will produce a signed attestation plus a tamper-evident hash summary of stored payloads and training manifests within 5 business days.

- Transfers & subprocessors: Redwood will apply SCCs for any transfer out of the EEA and will provide a subprocessor access map. If Customer elects EU-only deployment, Redwood will run the pilot in an EU Private instance and provide certificate of in-region processing.

Next steps I propose: (1) Elena/team confirm you’re ok with the draft summary above, (2) Rachel/Marcus to insert the formal addendum into Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, (3) we circulate DocuSign (link below) for signatures and, if requested, schedule a 30-minute SIG to walk the privacy team through the evidence package format.

DocuSign (proposed envelope): https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123456789
Drive proof packet (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/medinnovate/DPA_v3

If that plan works I’ll ask Legal Ops to prepare the addendum and route it for signature.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
